name: Peace is Elusive the Harder You Look For It
excerpt: By going inside your body, You may know the whole world. By looking at your own soul, You may see through the windows of heaven.
body:
By going inside your body,
You may know the whole world.
By looking at your own soul,
You may see through the windows of heaven.
The further you travel to find peace,
The more elusive it becomes.
Therefore, the sage learns without leaving,
Sees without looking
And all is achieved with non-action.

name: Creation, in its Totality, is Harmonious
excerpt: The sage’s mind is the mind of nature. He has no mind of his own. He accepts the light and the dark. He accepts the true and the false.
body:
The sage’s mind is the mind of nature.
He has no mind of his own.
He accepts the light and the dark.
He accepts the true and the false.
The sage sees creation as a harmonious whole.

name: Keep Your Life in Order
excerpt: Be prepared for anything to happen. The master follows the saying: “Live each day like it will be the last, For one day you will be right.”
body:
Be prepared for anything to happen.
The master follows the saying:
“Live each day like it will be the last,
For one day you will be right.”

When you accept that you will die,
You can truly begin to live.
Settle your affairs at the end of each day.
Tie up your loose ends before bed each night.
Keep your life in order
So you do not leave a mess behind.

The sage is ready for death,
As he is ready for retiring to bed.
He looks back on his life
Like a good day of work.

name: The Tao Produces, But Not Possesses
excerpt: The Tao gives birth to all things. It nourishes them, teaches them, shapes them, And guides them to reach their true expression.
body:
The Tao gives birth to all things.
It nourishes them, teaches them, shapes them,
And guides them to reach their true expression.
Therefore, all things honor the Tao by their existence.
The Tao produces, but not possesses,
It gives to all, but doesn’t take.
Though it guides, it interferes with none.

name: Seal Your Senses, Quiet Your Mind
excerpt: At the beginning of the Universe Was the Tao. Study the Tao and you’ll understand All that flow from it.
body:
At the beginning of the Universe
Was the Tao.
Study the Tao and you’ll understand
All that flow from it.

Understand what flows from it,
But remember the Source.
Practice its ways and
You will have harmony.

If your mind races and
You chase desires;
Your heart will not rest.

Seal your senses,
Quiet your mind,
Do not overwork and
You will know peace.

Turn your eyes inward.
Find the light inside of you.
Yield to the natural way and
You will merge with the source of all things.

name: Treat Others as Yourself
excerpt: The man that masters grounding Cannot be uprooted. When he knows how to find his center, He cannot float away.
body:
The man that masters grounding
Cannot be uprooted.
When he knows how to find his center,
He cannot float away.

If you cultivate your inner spirit,
Your virtue will shine clearly.
If your virtue shines clearly,
Your family will flourish.
If your family flourishes,
Your village will prosper.
If your village prospers,
Then your nation will be abundant.

Thus, the sage sees others as if he were them.
He treats other families as if it were his family,
He deals with other villages as his village.
And thus all nations are treated the same as his nation.
Follow the Tao, let it flow through you;
The best chance for peace on earth.

name: Become Like an Infant
excerpt: To merge with the Tao Is to become like an infant. Their body is soft but full of energy.
body:
To merge with the Tao
Is to become like an infant.
Their body is soft but full of energy.
They know nothing
Of merging yin and yang inside themselves,
But yet their bodies pulse with original energy.
They can play and laugh all day long,
But never grow tired,
Because they have inner harmony.

Inner harmony is strong and eternal,
And a raging mind is reflective
Of a being a war with himself.

name: Don’t Try to Control
excerpt: Lead by example, Demonstrate by following the Tao. Don’t try to control.
body:
Lead by example,
Demonstrate by following the Tao.
Don’t try to control.

Let matters govern themselves.
The more rules there are,
The more rules will be broken.
The more guards there are,
The more insecure people will be.

The cleverer the rules try to be,
The stranger things become.

Therefore, the wise leader says:
If I leave people alone,
They will transform themselves.
If I allow quietude,
The people will find regular routines.
If I don’t interfere,
The people will become prosperous.
If I have no desires,
The people will return to simplicity.

name: Be Bright, But Not Flashy
excerpt: When the leader governs lightly, The people are at ease. When the leader governs harshly, The people become crafty. The sage is wise, but not cunning.
body:
When the leader governs lightly,
The people are at ease.
When the leader governs harshly,
The people become crafty.
The sage is wise, but not cunning.
He is sharp, but not cutting,
He makes is point, but is not demeaning.
He is bright but is not flashy.

name: Too Mush Fussing Ruins The Process
excerpt: Ruling a small country is like frying a small fish. You will ruin it with too much fussing and flipping.
body:
Ruling a small country is like frying a small fish.
You will ruin it with too much fussing and flipping.
Govern your country like the Tao governs creation and
Negative ways cannot harm the people.
If evil has nothing to oppose, it loses its power.
When opposites will no longer harm each other,
Both are in accord with the Tao.

name: A Great Man Must be Humble and Yielding
excerpt: A great nation is like a mighty river valley. People, goods, and services all flow to it. The more powerful it becomes, The more humble it must be.
body:
A great nation is like a mighty river valley.
People, goods, and services all flow to it.
The more powerful it becomes,
The more humble it must be.

A great nation is like a great man.
He too must become humble and yielding.
When he harms another, he must make it right.

His greatest enemy stares at him in the mirror.
If a man and a nation are centered in the Tao,
They serve the world and nourish people.
They can be a light to all that see them.

name: Focus on Health Before You’re Sick
excerpt: Practice non-doing. Observe without action. The biggest problem in the world Could have been solved when it was small.
body:
Practice non-doing.
Observe without action.
The biggest problem in the world
Could have been solved when it was small.

Focus on your health
Before you become sick.
Accomplish great tasks
One small action at a time.

The sage is never doing things for greatness,
Yet achieves greatness
Through completing the simple.

If you face difficulties squarely,
You find no difficulty at all.

name: There is no shortcut to lasting enlightenment
excerpt: It is easy to grasp something at rest. Plans are easy to make in advance. Trouble can be overcome before it starts. Set things in order before chaos erupts.
body:
It is easy to grasp something at rest.
Plans are easy to make in advance.
Trouble can be overcome before it starts.
Set things in order before chaos erupts.

The oak springs from the acorn.
A sky scraper begins with a pile of dirt.
The journey of 1,000 miles begins with a single step.
Rushing to completion can lead to failure.

Only a fool tries to get something for nothing.
There is no shortcut to lasting enlightenment.
Therefore, the sage watches patiently as things unfold.
He is as tranquil on the first mile as on the 1,000th mile.

Unattached to the outcome, he has nothing to lose.
People usually fail when success is just around the corner.
Thus, have enthusiasm at the end just as at the beginning.

Desire to remain desire-less. Do not collect things.
Let go of fixed notions. Come back to what you have lost.
Help things regain their original nature,
But do so without interfering.

name: A Simple Life is Easiest to Live
excerpt: In old times, the sages taught by example. When you think you know, You can’t be taught. When your mind is open, You can sense the Way for yourself.
body:
In old times, the sages taught by example.
When you think you know,
You can’t be taught.
When your mind is open,
You can sense the Way for yourself.

To be a leader, forget cleverness and cunning.
A simple life is the easiest to live.
When you are content,
You become an example
Of how to live your true nature.

name: To Help People, Be Humble
excerpt: The ocean is bigger than all streams Because it sits below them.
body:
The ocean is bigger than all streams
Because it sits below them.

If you want to help people,
You have to demonstrate humility.
Listen with your whole heart.
Speak like a subordinate.
Give with both hands.
Learn how to follow.

The master is above all the people,
Though no one feels his weight.

name: A Great Warrior Does Not Seek War
excerpt: A great fighter remains calm in the battle. A great winner does not flaunt his victory. A great leader lifts up the people. This is the virtue of not striving.
body:
A great fighter remains calm in the battle.
A great winner does not flaunt his victory.
A great leader lifts up the people.
This is the virtue of not striving.
This is how to lead people.
This is the union of man and Tao.

name: The Best Military Strategists Yield
excerpt: Military strategists advise That it is better to be patient Than to make the first move.
body:
Military strategists advise
That it is better to be patient
Than to make the first move.

It is better to withdraw a foot
Than to go forward an inch.

This is the art of moving without advancing.
Pulling back without using force.
Facing the fight without engaging the enemy.

Underestimating the enemy will lead to disaster.
When two forces engage in battle,
The one that yields will win.

name: Study the Patterns Inside Yourself
excerpt: The Tao is easy to understand And easy to put into practice. Yet no one knows it And no one practices it.
body:
The Tao is easy to understand
And easy to put into practice.
Yet no one knows it
And no one practices it.

How can you know the Tao?
By looking inside yourself.
How can you grasp the Tao?
By studying the patterns of nature.

Studying the patterns of nature is very rare.
Looking inside oneself is rarer still.
This is why the Tao is mostly unheard of.

name: Do the Tao to Learn It
excerpt: When people lose their sense of awe, Science explains the five sense world. When they don’t know how to care for themselves, They turn to doctors to tell them how to act.
body:
When people lose their sense of awe,
Science explains the five sense world.
When they don’t know how to care for themselves,
They turn to doctors to tell them how to act.

The sage observes from a distance.
He doesn’t meddle in peoples affairs.
Yet, like the eternal Tao, he teaches by example.
To learn it, they simply have to do it.

name: Savor Each Moment
excerpt: If you no longer fear death, Is there anything to be afraid of? Accept the impermanence of things Savor each moment. When you resist natural law, You try to replace the Great Tao.
body:
If you no longer fear death,
Is there anything to be afraid of?
Accept the impermanence of things
Savor each moment.
When you resist natural law,
You try to replace the Great Tao.
You don’t have the energy to replace the Great Tao
And you will only end up exhausted.

name: A Wise Leader Trusts the People
excerpt: When the leaders are greedy The people do not have time for joy. When people have no money for themselves They begin to grow restless.
body:
When the leaders are greedy
The people do not have time for joy.
When people have no money for themselves
They begin to grow restless.
A wise ruler knows to trust the people,
Let them work in joy and
There will be enough for everyone.

name: Yielding Overcomes that which is Immovable
excerpt: Water is the softest and Most yielding substance. Thus, it can dissolve the hard and immovable.
body:
Water is the softest and
Most yielding substance.
Thus, it can dissolve the hard and immovable.

The soft dissolves the hard,
That which yields can overcome
That which is immovable.
In this, water has no equal.

But who practices this in life?
The sage takes the low spots and
Thieves don’t trouble him.
He lives a simple life and
His years are beyond measure.

name: Practice Forgiveness
excerpt: Arguments Between People Can leave bitter resentments. How can the relationship return To a healthy state of affairs?
body:
Arguments Between People
Can leave bitter resentments.
How can the relationship return
To a healthy state of affairs?

The sage performs his part of the obligation.
He does not demand justice
On the part of the other.

The virtuous take care
Of their responsibilities.
The virtue-less know only
Blaming and fault-finding.

Meanwhile, the Great Tao is impartial.

name: Nourish Gently, Lead Quietly
excerpt: The wise man does not have To be right or win an argument. The virtuous man is not interested In finding fault.
body:
The wise man does not have
To be right or win an argument.
The virtuous man is not interested
In finding fault.

When you know everything,
There is nothing left to learn.
When you have more than you need,
Its presence weighs you down.
Therefore, the sage does not hoard.
He gives freely and always has plenty.
The Tao nourishes gently and
The master leads quietly.

Flow like water,
Reflect like a mirror,
Respond like an echo.

name: Talking Does not Cause Enlightenment
excerpt: Practices that are complicated Are not the practices that lead to wholeness.
body:
Practices that are complicated
Are not the practices that lead to wholeness.

Words can help the mind feel at ease,
But talking does not cause enlightenment.

From the oneness, energy is pure and whole.
Once individuated, it polarizes.
Harmonizing polarity,
The alchemist returns to oneness.
Living in polarity,
There is only struggle.

Oneness and polarity
Come from the same source.
This source is the Tao.
But who can describe the Tao?
Who can name the source of all things?

name: Thoughts Are Like Geese, Flying over a Lake
excerpt: Judging yourself causes Separation between right and wrong. Right and wrong creates shame or pride And an inner shadow.
body:
Judging yourself causes
Separation between right and wrong.
Right and wrong creates shame or pride
And an inner shadow.

Labeling thoughts, words, or deeds,
As acceptable or unacceptable
Takes one from wholeness and integrity
Into light and darkness.

Therefore, follow the pattern of virtue
Set forth by nature.
Let your heart shine joy and love to all,
Like the Sun towards the Earth.

Watch your judgments, shame,
And pride float by,
Like a lake watches a flock of geese fly over.

In this way, the Sage allows
The coming and going of people, thoughts, and energy
Without grasping, without gain or loss.
Because of this, he is at peace.

name: Achieve That Which Really Matters
excerpt: If you give away your power To experts, possessions, or thoughts, Your body will weaken.
body:
If you give away your power
To experts, possessions, or thoughts,
Your body will weaken.

If you trade your health for money,
You’ll want to trade it back one day.

The alchemist leads his life
By emptying his mind,
Filling his belly, decreasing his desires,
And strengthening his bones.

In this way, he loses material possessions,
But he gains his health and peace of mind.
By giving up clever desires,
He doesn’t spend energy
Chasing passing fads.

Practicing non-doing,
He achieves that which really matters.

name: Tao in the Body as a River to the Sea
excerpt: The Sage hard-wires himself Into the inexhaustible nature of the Tao.
body:
The Sage hard-wires himself
Into the inexhaustible nature of the Tao.

The five elements and yin/yang
Exist without end.

Finding the Tao in the body
Is like a river finding the sea.

What is the pattern of the inner and outer?
Merge the above and below,
You will experience the Great Mystery.

name: Tune to the Frequency of Creation
excerpt: The Tao doesn’t see Right and wrong. All things have equal weight To heaven and earth.
body:
The Tao doesn’t see
Right and wrong.
All things have equal weight
To heaven and earth.

The Alchemist sees polarity
As two aspects of the same energy.

Practicing the Tao gives energy.
Practicing in the world steals energy.
The Tao is ever present, but is inexhaustible.
Tuning in, it is always there.

name: The Tao: Ever Present, Yet Rarely Found
excerpt: Giving birth to all things, The Tao is the mother of creation. Having been birthed by the Tao, It is inside of us all. It is ever present, But is rarely found.
body:
Giving birth to all things,
The Tao is the mother of creation.
Having been birthed by the Tao,
It is inside of us all.
It is ever present,
But is rarely found.

Searching inside,
The alchemist finds it
And turns lead into gold.

name: Do Not Strive
excerpt: Nature is infinite and eternal. How is nature infinite? It has no beginning.
body:
Nature is infinite and eternal.
How is nature infinite?
It has no beginning.

How is nature eternal?
It has no end.
It has no desires,
Therefore it is always present.

The alchemist does not strive,
Thus he is satisfied.
He does not pursue safety and security,
Yet he has all he needs.

name: A Simple Life Leads to Clarity
excerpt: The Tao is like water, nourishing all things. Water flows in the low places And always finds its way home.
body:
The Tao is like water, nourishing all things.
Water flows in the low places
And always finds its way home.

The alchemist accepts what is discarded
And recycles energy to benefit all.

He lives a simple life,
Therefore his mind is clear.
Because he is not taking,
He is able to give.

He speaks with clarity,
Because he knows himself.
As a leader, he encourages people
To choose their own destiny.

When taking action,
He applies his best gifts,
And then lets go.
By not striving for more,
He is content,
And people feel safe around him.

(C. Lemunyon, photographer)

name: When You Have Enough, Relax
excerpt: When you are over-doing, You become exhausted.
body:
When you are over-doing,
You become exhausted.

Continue fussing over your work,
And you will spoil it.

Chase after more, better, and different,
You will never relax.

By seeking people’s approval,
It is never found.

Know when you have enough, relax.
This is the only way to peace.

name: Give, Be Unattached to the Outcome
excerpt: Can your body, soul, and personality Function as one?
body:
Can your body, soul, and personality
Function as one?

Will you practice ancient wisdom
And rejuvenate your body?

Growing the good inside you,
Can you purify all the bad?

In your personal relationships,
Can you approach them with love and compassion?

Can you deal with the most important events
By allowing them to find their own path?

Connecting clearly with nature,
Will you release your ego to see the truth in all things?

Giving, creating, releasing, and loving
While being unattached to the outcome;
This is the supreme virtue.

name: Nurture Your Inner Essence
excerpt: The skin, the hair, and the nails give us our beauty But the inner essence makes the body move.
body:
The skin, the hair, and the nails give us our beauty
But the inner essence makes the body move.

The bones are known for their hard and lasting nature,
But the marrow inside gives them their life.

Exercise makes the muscles strong and appealing,
But the quality of chi is the quality of life.

The world focuses on the outside,
But the alchemist cultivates the inside.

name: Turn Your Senses Inward
excerpt: Constantly looking outward, Exhausts the eyes and liver.
body:
Constantly looking outward,
Exhausts the eyes and liver.

Over-reaching to listen,
Exhausts the ears and kidneys.

Eating too much numbs the tongue,
And burdens the stomach and spleen.

Compulsive thinking of past and future
Will drive a person crazy.

An unquenchable desire for more
Will break the heart.

Therefore, the alchemist turns his senses inward.
He feels the ebb and flow of creation
But maintains his center.

name: Be Content With What you Have
excerpt: Gain and loss can both drain our energy. Hope and regret both steal the present moment.
body:
Gain and loss can both drain our energy.
Hope and regret both steal the present moment.

How do gain and loss both drain our energy?
When you gain, you have to hold on to it.
When you lose, you lament what is gone.

How do hope and regret both steal the present moment?
Hopes for the future can leave us discontented.
Regret is a fool’s errand, as the past can’t be rewritten.

Therefore, the alchemist is content with what he has.
If he thinks of the past, the focus is on lessons learned.

Rather than regret past mistakes,
He can focus on love for others
And forgiveness of self
When thoughts of the past arise.
Keep your mind with your body,
Allow true virtue to arise.

name: Chase the Tao and You’ll Never Catch It
excerpt: Who can see what can’t be seen? Who can hear what can’t be heard? Who can feel what can’t be touched?
body:
Who can see what can’t be seen?
Who can hear what can’t be heard?
Who can feel what can’t be touched?

Through the practice of subtle energy, the alchemist fuses his senses.
Through the fusion of his senses, he grasps the formless.

The Tao is not bright and not dim. It has no beginning and no end.
Chase it and you’ll never catch it. It is elusive, but it is available everywhere.
Merge with it, though, and you move with the present.

You can’t know it, but you can be it.
Live as the Tao lives. This is the way to peace.

name: Can You Yield Until Your Mind is Clear?
excerpt: The Taoist masters of old were wise and lived in harmony. Their minds were deep and they kept their skills hidden.
body:
The Taoist masters of old were wise and lived in harmony.
Their minds were deep and they kept their skills hidden.
Because their minds can’t be fathomed and their skills were hidden,
How can we understand them?

They were careful, like one standing on slippery rocks.
They were alert, like a sniper looking through his rifle’s scope.
They were polite, like a visitor in a foreign land.
They flowed like an ancient river.
They were as flexible as the potter’s clay.
They bent like the willow in the storm,
Their minds were as clear as
A mirror reflecting the summer night.

Can you yield, give, and bend until your mind is clear?
Can you exhibit the patience needed,
To allow inner virtue to arise by itself?
One who merges with the Tao
Doesn’t seek to enforce his will.

By letting things take their natural course,
We become like the old masters in modern times.

name: All Things Return to the Tao
excerpt: Allow your thoughts to leave your head. Let your heart forget its desires. Watch the drama of the world unfold And contemplate its return to the origin.
body:
Allow your thoughts to leave your head.
Let your heart forget its desires.
Watch the drama of the world unfold
And contemplate its return to the origin.

All things return to the Tao.
By allowing this process,
You find serenity.
The return to the source creates quietness inside.

The enlightened understand this journey.
This understanding allows tolerance.
Practicing tolerance, you become impartial.
Being impartial, you see the oneness of all things.
Seeing the oneness of all things, you merge with the Tao.
Merging with the Tao, you become eternal.

name: Temporary Defeat v. Failure
excerpt: Temporary defeat is like encountering a detour on our way to work. Failure is like a car breakdown that prevents us from making it to work at all—and then we quit at the side of…
body:
Temporary defeat is like encountering a detour on our way to work. Failure is like a car breakdown that prevents us from making it to work at all—and then we quit at the side of the road and our dream of getting to work dies.

Zig Ziglar used to say that “we don’t drown if we fall in water, we only drown if we stay there.” As we encounter setbacks, we need to honestly analyze if this is a temporary defeat that we will learn and grow from, or if this will be the failure that means the end of this particular project, goal, career, or relationship.

We can rebound from temporary defeat, we cannot rebound from failure. We can often choose which it will be.

name: Trust People and They Become Trustworthy
excerpt: The sage understands leadership And the people choose their own fate.
body:
The sage understands leadership
And the people choose their own fate.

Another type of leader works for love and praise.
The next type of leader manages through fear.
And the final type of leader is despised.

It is by trusting the people that they become trustworthy.
Setting the example through action,
The wise leader lets the people have the credit.

name: When the Tao is Forgotten, Chaos Emerges
excerpt: When you forget the Tao, You focus only on being a good person. When you forget to be a good person, Intelligence becomes the strongest asset.
body:
When you forget the Tao,
You focus only on being a good person.
When you forget to be a good person,
Intelligence becomes the strongest asset.

When intelligence is the strongest asset,
Cleverness and fabrication emerge.
Cleverness and fabrication replace peace.
When there is no peace, chaos emerges.
A state in chaos is taken over by selfish men.

name: Focus on Simplicity, Invest in What Lasts
excerpt: Forget your mind, Your body will be happier.
body:
Forget your mind,
Your body will be happier.

Forget laws,
Focus on doing the right thing.

Forget material riches,
Store up gold inside of you.

The superficial aspects of life should be subordinated.
Focus on simplicity and invest in what lasts.

name: Stop Thinking and Your Problems Cease
excerpt: What is the difference between good and bad? Who decides what is right and wrong? Is it necessary to fear what others fear?
body:
What is the difference between good and bad?
Who decides what is right and wrong?
Is it necessary to fear what others fear?

Everyone is running about, trying to get it all done today.
The alchemist is unmoved, like a baby before it learns to smile.
He is waiting, as if there is nowhere to go.

Others try storing up goods;
The alchemist seems simple.
Others want to be bright and flashy;
The alchemist seems dark.
Others have to be on alert;
The alchemist is as calm as the ocean depths.
Others discuss their ways and means;
The alchemist seems unsophisticated.

He is different than others.
He relies on the Tao.

name: The Way of Health is to follow the Tao
excerpt: That is why the alchemist possesses radiance. How can he follow the Tao, if it is un-graspable?
body:
That is why the alchemist possesses radiance.
How can he follow the Tao, if it is un-graspable?

He can follow it because
He doesn’t try to hold it like a dogma.

If the Tao is dark and vast, how can he be radiant?
He is radiant because the Tao is the source of health.

The Tao was present before creation.
How does the alchemist know this?
He knows by looking inside himself.

name: Acknowledge Your Fragments to Become Whole
excerpt: See your crookedness to become straight. Empty yourself to become full. Abandon your fear of death to become truly alive. Give up your possessions to receive what truly matters.
body:
See your crookedness to become straight.
Empty yourself to become full.
Abandon your fear of death to become truly alive.
Give up your possessions to receive what truly matters.
The alchemist sees polarities as points on the same continuum.

Without trying, you can shine brightly for all to see.
By not trying to prove yourself, you become trustworthy.
When you forget who you are, people recognize themselves in you.
When you don’t have to win an argument, you will become happy.

It is not idle chatter that the ancients said
“By acknowledging your fragments, you become whole.”
When you see your flaws, you can heal them.

name: Simple Words Can Transmit the Message
excerpt: To learn this, study nature. A fierce tornado won’t last all morning. Neither does a sudden downpour continue all day.
body:
To learn this, study nature.
A fierce tornado won’t last all morning.
Neither does a sudden downpour continue all day.

The Tao is the architect of nature.
If the great Tao cannot make fierce and sudden things last,
What hope does man have of sustaining force and temper?
Therefore, if you merge with nature,
Your actions follow the Tao.

If you open yourself to virtue, virtue will flow through you.
If you allow yourself to yield, you can learn what forcefulness cannot.

Open yourself to natural ways.
Follow the path of the Tao.
Your life will become much easier.

name: When You Try to Shine, You Dim Your Light
excerpt: You are unproductive.
body:
When your energy is in your head,

You are ungrounded.

When you hurry,

You are unproductive.

When you try to shine,

You dim your light.

This is like eating too much food, or

A traveler with too much baggage.

To follow the Way is to abstain from overindulgence.

name: Far Away Means Returning
excerpt: What was present before the creation of all things? Still, silent, unchanging; it was the Mother of all things.
body:
What was present before the creation of all things?
Still, silent, unchanging; it was the Mother of all things.

I don’t know its name,
So I will call it Tao.
Tao means great.
Great means far.
Far means far away.
Far away means returning.

The sage can follow this pattern inside himself,
And thus return to the Tao.

name: Maintain Your Center
excerpt: Find your center of gravity And you will find lightness. Find serenity and you will notice Restlessness before it sets in.
body:
Find your center of gravity
And you will find lightness.
Find serenity and you will notice
Restlessness before it sets in.

You can travel all day,
Without losing the center of your being.
The sites, no matter how beautiful,
Don’t have to pull you away
From your inner awareness.

Many rush around the city,
Chasing this task and that.
To flit about in this manner
Takes away one’s center of gravity.
To chase temporal pleasures leads to restlessness.
Maintain a strong return address
In the center of your being.

Chen Wei Ming and Leung King Yu. Kungfu:

name: Any Situation Can Be a Tool for Learning
excerpt: To be relaxed in your spiritual journey, Be loose about the schedule and destination.
body:
To be relaxed in your spiritual journey,
Be loose about the schedule and destination.

To make your point of view be known,
Speak softly and listen to others point of view.

In making plans that benefit all,
Withdraw from calculations and schemes.

Like the sun and the earth,
The master is available to all.

Any situation can be a tool for learning and spiritual cultivation.
Recycle what is called bad energy,
And use it for the good of all.

This is embodying the natural way.

name: Emulate the Pattern of Nature
excerpt: Know how to be active with your practice, But rest and recover after. Emulate the mighty river Who follows its path spontaneously.
body:
Know how to be active with your practice,
But rest and recover after.
Emulate the mighty river
Who follows its path spontaneously.

Know how to shine brightly,
But keep to the darkness.
Emulate the pattern of nature
And the Tao will be strong inside of you.

Know the familiar,
But keep to the unfamiliar;
Accepting things as they are.

When you accept things as they are,
The Tao will shine inside you,
And you’ll return to your original nature.

name: How Long Has the Bright Moon Existed?
excerpt: I raise the wine cup to ask the sapphire sky What year is tonight in celestial palaces?
body:
I raise the wine cup to ask the sapphire sky
What year is tonight in celestial palaces?
I could ride the wind to return there
but fear the unbearable chill
high in jade towers with jeweled eaves

I dance with my crisp shadow
in delight known only to mortals
Circles painted pavilions
Seeps over carved doors
Shines on the sleepless

The moon has no regrets
Why does it glow in full over parted humans?
Misery and joy cycle as we separate and reunite
The moon wanes and waxes
Time forbids perfection
Let us live long to share moonlight’s spell
though a thousand miles apart

— Su Dongpo, Song poet, 1036-1101 CE

“Balance. Tai chi improves balance and, according to some studies, reduces falls. Proprioception — the ability to sense the position of one’s body in space — declines with age. Tai chi helps train this sense, which is a function of sensory neurons in the inner ear and stretch receptors in the muscles and ligaments. Tai chi also improves muscle strength and flexibility, which makes it easier to recover from a stumble. Fear of falling can make you more likely to fall; some studies have found that tai chi training helps reduce that fear.” https://www.health.harvard.edu/staying-healthy/the-health-benefits-of-tai-chi

Breathing down the sound of fire.

Here, alchemy begins.

name: Balance Exercises and Standing for Groundedness
excerpt: The mind focuses on the heaviness of the legs. To achieve this, naturally sink the chest and relax the tummy.
body:
The mind focuses on the heaviness of the legs. To achieve this, naturally sink the chest and relax the tummy. Rooting begins to form when we’re starting to feel relaxed in the standing pose.

Maintianing our balance is a skill that can serve us for a life time. Yoga or tai chi seems too intense? Do the exercise you see while using a chair for balance.

name: Being Content and Treating Lumbar Pain
excerpt: To Follow the Tao is to be Content When a man is in harmony with the Tao, He cultivates his health and practices virtue.
body:
To Follow the Tao is to be Content
When a man is in harmony with the Tao, He cultivates his health and practices virtue.
When a man forgets the about the Tao,
He forgets his health and focuses on selfish desires.
Selfish desires are born from the illusion of fear. Being selfish leads to the curse of discontentedness.
Greed can bring disaster
To a man’s health and reputation.
To follow the Tao is know
The satisfaction of being content.

Chi Kung for treating lumbar pain, cool since the 1500s and before!!

name: Tai Chi: Simple, Beatiful, Incredibly Effective
excerpt: Tai chi does not mean oriental wisdom or something exotic. It is the wisdom of your own senses, your own mind and body together as one process. ~Chungliang Al Huang
body:
Tai chi does not mean oriental wisdom or something exotic. It is the wisdom of your own senses, your own mind and body together as one process. ~Chungliang Al Huang

“It has long been my dream that one day Americans of all ages, creeds and colors will be practicing taijiquan in the parks of this nation as they do in China. Few places in the world have such beautiful open spaces which can and should be used productively at no expense. The result would be tremendous improvement in mental and physical well-being.” ~Jou Tsung Hwa

name: Finding Peace, Sun/Human Alchemy
excerpt: Peace is Elusive The Harder You Search By going inside your body, You may know the whole world. By looking at your own soul, You may see through the windows of heaven.
body:
Peace is Elusive
The Harder You Search
By going inside your body,
You may know the whole world.
By looking at your own soul,
You may see through the windows of heaven.
The further you travel to find peace, The more elusive it becomes.
Therefore, the sage learns without leaving, Sees without looking
And achieves all with non-action.

Connect to the fire of Nature

Face the sun, palms open.

Inhale its loving essence.

Exhale dark clouds from around the heart.

name: The Inner Smile and Tao of Pooh
excerpt: The Inner Smile: Bathe Your Organs in Resonate Colors and Positive Emotions (learn the Inner Smile; link in Bio.)
body:
The Inner Smile: Bathe Your Organs in Resonate Colors and Positive Emotions (learn the Inner Smile; link in Bio.)

Accept ‘what is’: the way of happiness.

name: Squatting and Merging with Stars
excerpt: Squatting can help many aspects of health. Start by holding to the back of a chair and then gradually go lower.
body:
Squatting can help many aspects of health. Start by holding to the back of a chair and then gradually go lower.

Our physical body can be an antennae for absorbing the energy of heavenly bodies. The “trick” is that a stronger connection with the earth, through a clear physical and emotional body, allows more celestial energy to be absorbed into the body. “Grow down to grow up.”

name: Non-Interference and Releasing Heat from the Heart
excerpt: The man of knowledge learns something every day. The man of Tao forgets something every day. Little by little, he lets go until nothing is done.
body:
Little is Accomplished by Interfering

The man of knowledge learns something every day. The man of Tao forgets something every day.
Little by little, he lets go until nothing is done. When nothing is done, everything is accomplished.
Everything is accomplished
When things follow their own course.
Little is accomplished by interfering.

Palms Exhale at the Heart
A teapot that’s full

Releases a little steam.

So too with the heart.

name: Simple Stretching for Self-Care
excerpt: Stretching doesn’t have to be complicated or painful to be very effective for the internal organs (#1), the spine (#2), and the major joints (#3).
body:
Stretching doesn’t have to be complicated or painful to be very effective for the internal organs (#1), the spine (#2), and the major joints (#3). Five minutes of stretching everyday goes a long way!

This stretching combination is great for the spine and front of the body. It’s yin/yang of opening and closing the body. Someday I hope mine look like these!

name: Connecting to your Center and the Earth, Massaging your Energy Channels
excerpt: Find your Center and Connect to the Earth, a path to health. (From Cosmic Healing Chi Kung by Mantak Chia.)
body:
Find your Center and Connect to the Earth, a path to health. (From Cosmic Healing Chi Kung by Mantak Chia.)

Trace the paths of the energy meridians to stimulate the flow of energy. (From the Healing Promise of Qi by Roger Jahnke.)

name: Your Health and Neutrality
excerpt: If you give away your power To experts, possessions, or thoughts, Your body will weaken.
body:
Achieve that Which Really Matters

If you give away your power
To experts, possessions, or thoughts,
Your body will weaken.

If you trade your health for money,
You’ll want to trade it back one day.

The alchemist leads his life
By emptying his mind,
Filling his belly, decreasing his desires,
And strengthening his bones.

In this way, he loses material possessions,
But he gains his health and peace of mind.
By giving up clever desires,
He doesn’t spend energy
Chasing passing fads.

Practicing non-doing,
He achieves that which really matters.

The Tao doesn’t see
Right and wrong.
All things have equal weight
To heaven and earth.

name: Tai Chi and Squatting Meditation
excerpt: The movements in qigong exercise all the joints of the body keeping it flexible and young.
body:
The movements in qigong exercise all the joints of the body keeping it flexible and young.

“As the practitioner incorporates the quality of tai chi movement into his life, he finds that he stops banging into things. The result of not falling into each step provides the opportunity to instantaneously ease back from unexpected barriers.” ~Wolfe Lowenthal

name: Massage Cervical Vertebrae,the Harmony of Creation
excerpt: To read his phone and tablet.
body:
Massage Cervical Vertebrae

Modern man leans in

To read his phone and tablet.

Stuck chi must escape.

Creation is Harmonious in its Totality
The sage’s mind is the mind of nature.

He has no mind of his own.
He accepts the light and the dark.
He accepts the true and the false.
The sage sees creation as a harmonious whole.

name: Just stretch.. just a little; then nothing
excerpt: Open the hips, stretch the hamstrings and calves. Just 30 seconds for the hips and 60 seconds for both legs.
body:
Open the hips, stretch the hamstrings and calves. Just 30 seconds for the hips and 60 seconds for both legs. We spend hours sitting; it just takes a few minutes to reverse that damage.

What if there was nothing to do?

name: A Wood Cutting on Internal Alchemy and Keeping Your Life in Order
excerpt: “Though their clothes are too tattered to keep out the cold, They’ll assure you they change all base metals to gold.” -An anonymous warning against alchemists, Ming Dynasty
body:
“Though their clothes are too tattered to keep out the cold,
They’ll assure you they change all base metals to gold.” -An anonymous warning against alchemists, Ming Dynasty

Woodcut illustration of ‘Putting the miraculous elixir on the tripod’ fromXingming guizhin (Pointers on Spiritual Nature and Bodily Life) by Yi Zhenren, a Daoist text on internal alchemy published in 1615 (3rd year of the Wanli reign period of Ming dynasty).

Keep Your Life in Order
Be prepared for anything to happen. The master follows the saying:
“Live each day like it will be the last, For one day you will be right.”
When you accept that you will die, You can truly begin to live.
Settle your affairs at the end of each day.
Tie up your loose ends before bed each night. Keep your life in order
So you do not leave a mess behind.
The sage is ready for death,
As he is ready for retiring to bed. He looks back on his life
Like a good day of work.

name: Embrace The Tree and The Tao Produces, but not Possesses
excerpt: Embrace The Tree and The Tao Produces, but not Possesses
body:
Embrace the Tree

Root beneath your feet,

Arms Hugging a Mighty Oak;

Thus Immovable.

excerpt: The Kidney Meridian: activate it with mediation, self-massage, herbs, and/or acupuncture… it will build vitality and make long-term deposits in your health!
body:
The Kidney Meridian: activate it with mediation, self-massage, herbs, and/or acupuncture… it will build vitality and make long-term deposits in your health!

Regrows tendons and ligaments.

Stretch like a cat does.

name: Tai chi is free and Seal your Senses
excerpt: www.luohan.com has these beautiful drawings demonstrating the principles of tai chi!! “Of all the exercises, I should say that T’ai Chi is the best.
body:
www.luohan.com has these beautiful drawings demonstrating the principles of tai chi!!
“Of all the exercises, I should say that T’ai Chi is the best. It can ward off disease, banish worry and tension, bring improved physical health and prolong life. It is a good hobby for your whole life, the older you are, the better. It is suitable for everyone – the weak, the sick, the aged, children, the disabled and blind. It is also an economical exercise. As long as one has three square feet of space, one can take a trip to paradise and stay there to enjoy life for thirty minutes without spending a single cent.” ~T.T. Liang (Liang Tung-Tsai, 1900-2002), T’ai Chi Ch’uan for Health and Self-Defense

Seal Your Senses, Quiet Your Mind
At the beginning of the Universe Was the Tao.
Study the Tao and you’ll understand All that flow from it.
Understand what flows from it, But remember the Source. Practice its ways and
You will have harmony.
If your mind races and You chase desires; Your heart will not rest.
Seal your senses, Quiet your mind,
Do not overwork and You will know peace.
Turn your eyes inward.
Find the light inside of you.
Yield to the natural way and
You will merge with the source of all things.
flags: Instagram spacer lines removed

name: The Yellow Emperor and Enlightenment
excerpt: Huang Di asked, “I’ve heard of people in ancient times, spoken of as the immortals, who knew the secrets of the universe and held the world in the palm of their hands.
body:
Huang Di asked, “I’ve heard of people in ancient times, spoken of as the immortals, who knew the secrets of the universe and held the world in the palm of their hands. They extracted essence from nature and practiced Qi Gong and various stretching and breathing exercises, and visualizations, to integrate body, mind and spirit. They remained undisturbed and thus attained extraordinary levels of accomplishment. Can you tell me about them?”
-The Yellow Emperor’s Classic of Medicine (the Neijing Suwen) ~240 B.C. translated by Maoshing Ni

The Yellow Emperor transmits medical books to Lei Gong: The Yellow Emperor, Huangdi, seated beneath a yellow canopy in the shade of a pine tree, flanked by four civil and military officials. is shown presenting books containing medical knowledge to Lei Gong, the Thunder Duke.

The Great Way Makes Sense
Walking on the Great Way
Is a path that makes sense.
The path of the Great Way
Is demonstrated by all aspects of nature.
It is a straight and easy path,
But people find many distractions.
Chasing fancy homes and expensive clothes Mean we neglect the spirit.
Many carry sharp weapons, But their minds are dull.
The senses are numbed
By excess food and drink,
And the Tao is all but forgotten Until the moment of death.

name: Hitting with Mung Beans and The Golden Rule
excerpt: Heals tendons, cools us.
body:
Modern man overheats

Mung bean bag absorbs toxins,

Heals tendons, cools us.

Treat Others as Yourself
The man that masters grounding Cannot be uprooted.
When he knows how to find his center, He cannot float away.
If you cultivate your inner spirit, Your virtue will shine clearly.
If your virtue shines clearly, Your family will flourish.
If your family flourishes,
Your village will prosper.
If your village prospers,
Then your nation will be abundant.
Thus, the sage sees others as if he were them. He treats other families as if it were his family, He deals with other villages as his village. And thus all nations are treated as his nation.
Follow the Tao, let it flow through you; The best chance for peace on earth.

name: Belt Chanel Meditation and Developing a Relationship with your Organs
excerpt: The belt channel meditation for psychic protection, grounding, and clarifying your inner space.
body:
The belt channel meditation for psychic protection, grounding, and clarifying your inner space.

Smile at your organs and they will smile back.

name: Wag More, Bark Less and Become Like and Infant
excerpt: “Wag More, Bark Less”
body:
“Wag More, Bark Less”

Shaking the head and wagging the tail to calm the heart. Release tension, steady nerves, elevate mood, optimize brain activities, strengthen leg muscles, and strengthen abdomen.

Become Like an Infant
To merge with the Tao
Is to become like an infant.
Their body is soft but full of energy.
They know nothing
Of merging yin and yang Inside themselves,
But yet their bodies pulse With original energy.
They can play and laugh all day long, But never grow tired,
Because they have inner harmony.
Inner harmony is strong and eternal, And a raging mind is reflective
Of a being at war with himself.

name: Tai Chi as Medicine and The Five Rites
excerpt: Tai chi is the one exercise that can universally help solve our growing health crisis. It has stood the test of thousands of years.
body:
Tai chi is the one exercise that can universally help solve our growing health crisis. It has stood the test of thousands of years. We have a generation of baby boomers with increasing health problems; old people who are sick, in pain, fearful, and cranky; a middle class that is increasingly incapable of affording most of the drugs that are prescribed for their ailments; children that are flaccid, diabetic and asthmatic. People of all ages are addicted to drugs, alcohol, sugar, cigarettes, and caffeine. Stress follows almost everyone like a shadow. ~Bruce Frantzis

“The benefits most likely to be achieved are increased energy, stress reduction, and an enhanced sense of calm, clarity of thought, increased strength and flexibility, resulting in an overall improvement in health and well-being.”

name: Stillness and Shaking
excerpt: (Qigong exercise to treat pain in the back, shoulders, arms)
body:
(Qigong exercise to treat pain in the back, shoulders, arms)

Let Your Body Be Still
If you know, you don’t speak. If you speak, you don’t know.
Close your mouth; Turn your ears inward.
Soften your sharp edges, Untie the knots in your belly and your soul.
Allow your eyes to receive, Let your body sit still. Unite into one whole.

Shaking the Body
Stagnate and dis-ease.
Shake loose stuck patterns and thoughts. Water moves, chi flows

name: Leadership and Tai Chi Opening Movement
excerpt: Don’t Try to Control Lead by example, Demonstrate leadership By following the Tao. Don’t try to control. Let matters govern themselves.
body:
Don’t Try to Control
Lead by example, Demonstrate leadership By following the Tao.
Don’t try to control.
Let matters govern themselves.
The more rules there are,
The more rules will be broken. The more guards there are,
The more insecure people will be. The cleverer the rules try to be, The stranger things become.
Therefore, the wise leader says: If I leave people alone,
They will transform themselves. If I allow quietude,
The people will find regular routines. If I don’t interfere,
The people will become prosperous. If I have no desires,
The people will return to simplicity.

Tai Chi Opening Movement
Raise hands, Earth rises.

Pull, push the whole universe.

Lower hands, sink in earth.

name: The Most Important Thing, The Snow of Yesterday
excerpt: The most important thing is to find out what is the most important thing. -Shunryu Suzuki
body:
The most important thing is to find out
what is the most important thing.
-Shunryu Suzuki

“The snow of yesterday
That fell like cherry blossoms
Is water once again”
-Gozan, 1789

name: Subtle Brightness and Deep roots
excerpt: Be Bright, But Not Flashy When the leader governs lightly, The people are at ease. When the leader governs harshly, The people become crafty. The sage is wise, but not cunning.
body:
Be Bright, But Not Flashy
When the leader governs lightly, The people are at ease.
When the leader governs harshly, The people become crafty.
The sage is wise, but not cunning. He is sharp, but not cutting.
He makes his point, But is not demeaning. He is bright
But is not flashy.

Photo: luohan.com

Finding the Source is Like
Having Deep Roots
A ruler who follows the Tao Governs with frugality.
To be frugal is to live with moderation. Moderation means to return before straying.
To return before straying Is to find the source.
Finding the source
Is like having deep, firm roots.

name: Inner Cultivation and the Big Picture
excerpt: At the higher stages of energy continuation, one will find his movements are now being governed by the movement of his internal energy. ~Wu Ta-yeh
body:
At the higher stages of energy continuation, one will find his movements are now being governed by the movement of his internal energy. ~Wu Ta-yeh

“You are not a drop in the ocean. You are the entire ocean in a drop” – Rumi

name: Deep Roots, Tai Chi with a Tree
excerpt: Tai Chi Push, Sink Back Hands move in tai chi,
body:
Tai Chi Push, Sink Back
Hands move in tai chi,

Hips open, close, moving lymph.

Feet rock heel to toe.

Tai Chi With a Tree
Trade energy with a Tree.
Like O2 and CO2.
Roots grip. Trees: the great teachers.

name: Meditation and Happiness
excerpt: “Expert meditators with more than 10,000 hours of practice showed the greatest activity in the limbic systems and appeared to have permanently altered their brains to generate…
body:
“Expert meditators with more than 10,000 hours of practice showed the greatest activity in the limbic systems and appeared to have permanently altered their brains to generate positive thoughts. Even outside of meditation, committed meditators permanently changed the way their brains operated.”

https://www.naturalnews.com/030442_meditation_happiness.html

Too Mush Fussing Ruins The Process
Ruling a country
Is like frying a small fish. You will ruin it with too much Fussing and flipping.
Govern your country
Like the Tao governs creation
And negative ways cannot harm the people.
If evil has nothing to oppose,
It loses its power.
When opposites no longer harm each other, Both are in accord with the Tao.

name: Internal Alchemy, Humility
excerpt: Humanity’s Purpose? Internal Alchemy:
body:
Humanity’s Purpose?
Internal Alchemy:

Blend energies; transform base desires

To spiritual virtue.

A Great Man Must be Humble and Yielding
A great nation is like a mighty river valley. People, goods, and services all flow to it. The more powerful it becomes,
The more humble it must be.
A great nation is like a great man.
He too must become humble and yielding. When he harms another, he must make it right.
His greatest enemy stares at him in the mirror. If a man and a nation are centered in the Tao, They serve the world and nourish people. They can be a light to all that see them.

name: Resonance and Cultivation
excerpt: “The tone of musical instruments and our own voice facilitate deepening the resonance of our body-mind with the universal rhythms and wholeness of spirit.
body:
“The tone of musical instruments and our own voice facilitate deepening the resonance of our body-mind with the universal rhythms and wholeness of spirit. Yogic practices of rhythmic breath and devotion, chanting and singing, or other forms of gentle movement such as T’ai chi, promote integration…. As we align more closely with our own rhythm, serendipity is a frequent visitor as we resonate more closely with the rhythms of the universe.” ~JoEllen Goertz Koerner, “Quantum Healing,” Healing Presence: The Essence of Nursing, 2011 (2nd edition)

“Through cultivating your inner Qi, you become strong, not as an “individual” against the world but as an integral part of the world….” ~Garri Garripoli, Qigong: Essence of the Healing Dance

name: Earth’s Energy Rises to Nourish the Body
excerpt: Massage the “five earth gates” referenced in the photo. The Kidney-1 points at the ball of the foot, the Pericardium-8 points at the centers of the palms of the hands, and the tan…
body:
Massage the “five earth gates” referenced in the photo. The Kidney-1 points at the ball of the foot, the Pericardium-8 points at the centers of the palms of the hands, and the tan tien point just below the navel. Then, allow/envision the earth’s energy flowing into the body through these points. It can be stored in the navel, the organs, the bones, the tendons, etc.

Photo: Awaken Healing Light of the Tao, Mantak Chia

The kidneys are the batteries of the body. In meditation, invite the Earth’s Energy to rise up through the balls of the feet, along the inside of the legs (the Kidney Meridian), and into the kidneys themselves. Recharge the body; no cost!

name: Share the Tao and Massage the Kidneys
excerpt: Share the Tao With All All things flow from the Tao.
body:
Share the Tao With All
All things flow from the Tao.

It is the good man’s treasure.

It is the bad man’s safe haven.

Therefore, share the Tao with all.

The ancients revere it
Because it benefits everyone.

Massage the lower back to warm the kidneys, stimulate the adrenals in a healthy way, and to ease any discomfort of the lower lumbar.

name: Internal Weather, Focus on Your Health
excerpt: Fusion 1: Creation Cycle Internal seasons Match those that are external.
body:
Fusion 1: Creation Cycle
Internal seasons
Match those that are external.

Flow through five elements.

Focus on Health Before You’re Sick
Practice non-doing.
Observe without action.
The biggest problem in the world
Could have been solved when it was small.
Focus on your health Before you become sick. Accomplish great tasks One small action at a time.
The sage is never doing things for greatness, Yet achieves greatness
Through completing the simple.
If you face difficulties squarely, You find no difficulty at all.

excerpt: Massage the corners of the large intestine, drink plenty of water, squat a few times a day, and breathe deeply: this keeps your bowels moving.
body:
Massage the corners of the large intestine, drink plenty of water, squat a few times a day, and breathe deeply: this keeps your bowels moving.

Practice the Kidney Sound (Chooooo) to create gentleness, calmness, and stillness. It strengthens the ears, the bone marrow, and clears out fear. Try it!

Photo: Mantak Chia

name: Smile and Relax
excerpt: There is a lot of good inside of you. We all have demons, but we also have the God-ness and goodness inside of us.
body:
There is a lot of good inside of you. We all have demons, but we also have the God-ness and goodness inside of us. Try embracing all of the aspects of yourself, not judging them, giving them a voice, and empowering yourself to live the highest/purest/most virtuous version of yourself and all the aspects of yourself. The questions about the origin of souls and over-souls is important and fascinating at some level, but at another level it is just a mental exercise that may not take us as close toward feeling happy as a wet dog shaking water on us after a bath.

Don’t overthink life; just do actions that lead you to better feeling. Look for the good inside of you and let it grow. Find activities that help it grow. Plant a garden, help a neighbor, pick up trash, play music, pick up and gather groceries for an old person you know, watch dogs at the dog park, listen to musicians on the street, watch a sunrise or sunset with someone, visit your family, listen to your favorite music, and call your friends.

body:
“Qi gong therapy, as well as other branches of Chinese medicine, can be reduced to two simple principles: the cleansing of meridians to achieve harmonious energy flow, and the restoration of yin-yang balance.” ~Wong Kiew Kit

“To be inflexible to the change around you is to live in fear. Qigong is a useful tool to improve your flexibility, both mental and physical.” ~Garri Garripoli, Qigong: Essence of the Healing Dance

name: Lasting Enlightenment and Belt Channels
excerpt: There is no shortcut to lasting enlightenment It is easy to grasp something at rest. Plans are easy to make in advance. Trouble can be overcome before it starts.
body:
There is no shortcut to lasting enlightenment
It is easy to grasp something at rest. Plans are easy to make in advance. Trouble can be overcome before it starts. Set things in order before chaos erupts.
The oak springs from the acorn.
A sky scraper begins with a pile of dirt. The journey of 1,000 miles
Begins with a single step.
Only a fool tries to get something for nothing. There is no shortcut to lasting enlightenment.
So, the sage watches patiently as things unfold.
He is as tranquil on the 1st mile as the 1,000th mile.
Unattached to the outcome, he has nothing to lose. People can fail when success is around the corner. Thus, have enthusiasm at the end just as at the beginning.
Desire to remain desire-less. Do not collect things. Let go of fixed notions.
Come back to what you have lost.
Help things regain their original nature,
But do so without interfering.

Belt Channel Chi Kung
Create Boundaries.

Psychic buffers are vital.

Like Saturn’s rings.

excerpt: A Simple Life is Easiest to Live In old times, the sages taught by example. When you think you know, You can’t be taught.
body:
A Simple Life is Easiest to Live
In old times, the sages taught by example. When you think you know,
You can’t be taught.
When your mind is open,
You can sense the Way for yourself.
To be a leader, forget cleverness and cunning. A simple life is the easiest to live.
When you are content,
You become an example
Of how to live your true nature.

Core Channel
Left, right, and center.

Channels flow from root to crown.

Open the great rivers.

Massage the hands to release stress and prevent tension; not just in the hands, but in the whole body through the principles of reflexology.

name: Be Humble, The Tao is Practical
excerpt: To Help People, Be Humble The ocean is bigger than all streams Because it sits below them. If you want to help people, You have to demonstrate humility.
body:
To Help People, Be Humble
The ocean is bigger than all streams Because it sits below them.
If you want to help people,
You have to demonstrate humility.

Listen with your whole heart.

Speak like a subordinate.
Give with both hands.
Learn how to follow.
The master is above all the people, Though no one feels his weight.

The Tao is Practical
Many don’t understand the Tao.
And feel it’s impractical for the modern age.
For those that have looked inside themselves, The Tao is both understandable and practical.
When the Tao is put into practice,
The treasures become apparent.
The treasures are love, moderation, and yielding.
Love provides courage
And causes one to take healthy risks. It is victorious in attack
And impossible to defend.
Moderation ensures that You always have enough.
Yielding gives you peace of mind
And patience with friends and enemies.
If you have love for others, You are useful to the Tao.

name: Tendon Stretching, Skin Detoxing
excerpt: Iron Shirt 2, or Tendon Nei Kung, involves a series of moving postures that stretch and open tendons along the major tendon lines of the body.
body:
Iron Shirt 2, or Tendon Nei Kung, involves a series of moving postures that stretch and open tendons along the major tendon lines of the body. The major tendon lines that benefit are the pinkie, thumb, and tendons of the wrist. Tendons are connected throughout the body, so these postures create tendon strength and joint opening for the whole being.

This practice also includes a detoxifying method of gently hitting the tendons with a sock full of dry mung beans. Taoists classically used the mung bean hitter to absorb the heat the body produces which cannot be easily processed by the body. After excess heat is removed and the body is detoxified, the tendons are able to absorb higher frequencies of spiritual energy from the Inner Smile, Microcosmic Orbit, Fusion and Healing Love practices.

Two rattan sticks are taped together and used to detoxify the skin, nervous, and lymphatic systems. The sticks do not penetrate as deeply as the metal wire hitter, so their focus is not the bones but the layers of the skin. The rattan hitting practice is called ‘ringing the golden bell’ because the skin takes on a glowing, vibrant hue after being detoxified in this method.

name: Healing the Liver, Absorbing Chi through the Hair

name: The Tao is Practical, Not Striving

The Tao is Practical
Many don’t understand the Tao.
And feel it’s impractical for the modern age.
For those that have looked inside themselves, The Tao is both understandable and practical.
When the Tao is put into practice,
The treasures become apparent.
The treasures are love, moderation, and yielding.
Love provides courage
And causes one to take healthy risks. It is victorious in attack
And impossible to defend.
Moderation ensures that You always have enough.
Yielding gives you peace of mind
And patience with friends and enemies.
If you have love for others, You are useful to the Tao.

A Great Warrior Does Not Seek War
A great warrior does not seek war.
A great fighter remains calm in the battle. A great winner does not flaunt his victory. A great leader lifts up the people.
This is the virtue of not striving. This is how to lead people.
This is the union of man and Tao.

name: What is the Tao?
excerpt: Basically, I would summarize by saying that the Tao is about following the patterns of creation and of nature.
body: Basically, I would summarize by saying that the Tao is about following the patterns of creation and of nature. Humans, as part of creation and nature, have the patterns of creation and nature inside of us. However, unlike the rest of nature, humans also have free will and the ability to choose. (Trees, Rivers, and most undomesticated animals just naturally follow their true nature). Humans and society collectively don’t seem to choose to follow the patterns of nature. The study of Taoism, simply put, is a study of learning to reclaim the ability to live our true nature and be in harmony with the rest of creation. Does this make sense?

name: Friendship
excerpt: My dear friend and a poem he sent me. Rest In Peace, Randy England (1956-2018).
body:
My dear friend and a poem he sent me. Rest In Peace, Randy England (1956-2018).

I’ll miss the long emails, advice on the I-Ching, and drinking way too much tea when we got together. 🙏🏼

My friend lives high on East Mountain.
His nature is to love the hills and gorges.
In green spring he sleeps in empty woodland,
Still there when the noon sun brightens.
Pine-tree winds to dust his hair.
Rock-filled streams to cleanse his senses.
Free of all sound and stress,
Resting on a wedge of cloud and mist.

-Li Bai, Tang Dynasty, 701-762 CE

How long has the bright moon existed?

I raise the wine cup to ask the sapphire sky

What year is tonight in celestial palaces?

I could ride the wind to return there

but fear the unbearable chill

high in jade towers with jeweled eaves

I dance with my crisp shadow

in delight known only to mortals

Circles painted pavilions

Seeps over carved doors

Shines on the sleepless

The moon has no regrets

Why does it glow in full over parted humans?

Misery and joy cycle as we separate and reunite

The moon wanes and waxes

Time forbids perfection

Let us live long to share moonlight’s spell

though a thousand miles apart

— Su Dongpo, Song poet, 1036-1101 CE

name: Following the Tao and Health
excerpt: “There was a third type of a person, known as the sage. The sages lived peacefully under Heaven and Earth, following the rhythms of the planet and the universe.
body:
“There was a third type of a person, known as the sage. The sages lived peacefully under Heaven and Earth, following the rhythms of the planet and the universe. They adapted to society without being swayed by fashions and trends. They were free from emotional extremes and lived a balanced, contented existence. Their outward appearance, behavior and thinking did not reflect the conflicting norms of society. the sages appeared busy but were never depleted. Internally they did not overburden themselves. they abided in calmness, recognizing the empty nature of existence. The sages lived over one hundred years because they did not scatter or disperse their energies.

“A fourth type were the natural people who followed the Tao, the Way of Life, and were called naturalists. They lived in accordance with the rhythmic patters of the seasons: Heaven and Earth, moon, sun and stars. They aspired to follow the way of the ancient times, choosing not to lead excessive lifestyles. They, too, lived plainly and and enjoyed long life.”

name: Cosmic Nutrition and Yielding
excerpt: The ancient systems of nutritional healing regarded different foods as having different energetic qualities.
body:
“Food Energetics

The ancient systems of nutritional healing regarded different foods as having different energetic qualities. Just as yin and yang can be observed in a person’s energy, they can also be seen in food. Some foods are considered balancing: they do not have an extreme effect on energy but maintain the center. Other foods have an expanding quality: they expand chi and make us feel lighter. Other foods have a contracting quality: they contract chi, making us feel more grounded. We can understand these qualities better by considering a tree. A tree has a stable center: its trunk. It also has branches that reach upward to heaven and expand their energy out and roots that sink deep into the earth and contract the energy down.

We can use this model and apply it to different foods to understand their energetic qualities. Simple carbohydrates, which quickly release their sugars and thus rapidly lift our energy, are the most expansive foods. Complex carbohydrates also give us energy but are released more slowly. Thus they are expansive but less so. Fats and proteins have a contractive effect. They build our cells and have a grounding effect. Physiologically, fats and proteins slow the release of sugars in the diet and thus help to regulate blood sugar levels. The denser the food, the more contractive it is.”

Yielding Overcomes that Which is Immovable
Water is the softest and
Most yielding substance.
Thus, it can dissolve the hard and immovable.
The soft dissolves the hard, That which yields can overcome That which is immovable.
In this, water has no equal.
But who practices this in life? The sage takes the low spots and Thieves don’t trouble him.
He lives a simple life and
His years are beyond measure.

name: Nourosh Gently, After Enlightenment

body:
Nourish Gently, Lead Quietly

The wise man does not have
To be right or win an argument.

The virtuous man is not interested In finding fault.
When you know everything,
There is nothing left to learn.
When you have more than you need,

Its presence weighs you down.
Therefore, the sage does not hoard.

He gives freely and always has plenty.

The Tao nourishes gently and
The master leads quietly.
Flow like water,

Reflect like a mirror,

Respond like an echo.

After Enlightenment

When all the work is done

And lessons are embodied,

Throw the book away.

name: Musashi and Joseph Campbell on the Way
excerpt: Musashi and Joseph Campbell on the Way
body:
1. Accept everything just the way it is.
2. Do not seek pleasure for its own sake.
3. Do not, under any circumstances, depend on a partial feeling.
4. Think lightly of yourself and deeply of the world.
5. Be detached from desire your whole life long.
6. Do not regret what you have done.
7. Never be jealous.
8. Never let yourself be saddened by a separation.
9. Resentment and complaint are appropriate neither for oneself nor others.
10. Do not let yourself be guided by the feeling of lust or love.
11. In all things have no preferences.
12. Be indifferent to where you live.
13. Do not pursue the taste of good food.
14. Do not hold on to possessions you no longer need.
15. Do not act following customary beliefs.
16. Do not collect weapons or practice with weapons beyond what is useful.
17. Do not fear death.
18. Do not seek to possess either goods or fiefs for your old age.
19. Respect Buddha and the gods without counting on their help.
20. You may abandon your own body but you must preserve your honour.
21. Never stray from the Way.

Miyamoto Musashi

name: Talking Doesn’t Cause Enlightenment
excerpt: Thoughts Are Like Geese, Flying over a Lake Judging yourself causes Separation between right and wrong. Right and wrong creates shame or pride And an inner shadow.
body:
Thoughts Are Like Geese, Flying over a Lake
Judging yourself causes
Separation between right and wrong. Right and wrong creates shame or pride And an inner shadow.
Labeling thoughts, words, or deeds,
As acceptable or unacceptable
Takes one from wholeness and integrity Into light and darkness.
Therefore, follow the pattern of virtue Set forth by nature.
Let your heart shine joy and love to all, Like the Sun towards the Earth.
Watch your judgments, shame, And pride float by,
Like a lake watches
A flock of geese fly over.
In this way, the Sage allows
The coming and going of people, Thoughts, and energy
Without grasping, without gain or loss. Because of this, he is at peace.

Talking Does not Cause Enlightenment
Practices that are complicated
Are not the practices that lead to wholeness.
Words can help the mind feel at ease,
But talking does not cause enlightenment.
From the oneness, energy is pure and whole. Once individuated, it polarizes.
Living in polarity,
There is only struggle. Harmonizing polarity,
The alchemist returns to oneness.
Oneness and polarity
Come from the same source.
This source is the Tao.
But who can describe the Tao?
Who can merge with the source of all things?

name: Principles of Tai Chi, by Tung Ying Chieh
excerpt: “Tai Chi Chuan is an internal martial art exercise. Strength is produced in the bones. Power is reserved at the musclesm.
body:
Tung Ying Chieh

“Tai Chi Chuan is an internal martial art exercise. Strength is produced in the bones. Power is reserved at the musclesm. It does not require one to have tough skin or thick muscles, but sunken “chi” and strong bones are required. Therefore, learners have no suffering of broken bones and hurt muscles, and the tiredness of jumping, but just move naturally to find the potential of power of origin. It is an exercise to develop the your original power.”

“You can practice Tai Chi Chuan while you are walking, standing, sitting, and laying. The method is to use your mind to circulate the “chi”, and find the feeling. For example: to feel the difference between holding a tea cup with strength, and without strength; to feel the difference of walking with heavy steps, and with light steps. When you are standing still, try to feel the difference of straightening your legs, and bending your legs; one leg, or two legs on the ground.”

name: The Pineal Gland, Turning Inward
excerpt: “The pineal is an endocrine gland sitting alone in the brain, level with our eyes. The pineal gland produces melatonin and regulates our daily and seasonal circadian rhythms.
body:
Here are some ways to Activate the Pineal Gland:

  1. Spend time in the sunlight every day
  2. Sleep in complete Darkness
  3. Commit to a regular meditation practice as this will develop and enhance your pineal gland

“The pineal is an endocrine gland sitting alone in the brain, level with our eyes. The pineal gland produces melatonin and regulates our daily and seasonal circadian rhythms. Melatonin is the chemical in charge of our sleep cycles and the quality of our sleep, and it also regulates the onset of puberty. Melatonin is responsible for fighting against free radicals. A decline in melatonin triggers the ageing process in the body. Serotonin, the neurotransmitter or happy chemical responsible for our mood, is transformed into melatonin only in the pineal gland. The pineal plays a major role in hibernation of animals, in metabolism and seasonal breeding.”

From Awaken Healing Light of the Tao, by Mantak Chia

Tao Te Ching #14

Chase the Tao and You’ll Never Catch It
Who can see what can’t be seen? Who can hear what can’t be heard? Who can feel what can’t be touched?
Through the practice of subtle energy, the alchemist fuses his senses. Through the fusion of his senses,
he grasps the formless.
The Tao is not bright and not dim.
It has no beginning and no end.
Chase it and you’ll never catch it.
It is elusive, but it is available everywhere. Merge with it and you move with the present.
You can’t know it, but you can be it.
Live as the Tao lives. This is the way to peace.

Tao te Ching: #13

Be Content With What you Have
Gain and loss can both drain our energy.
Hope and regret both steal the present moment.
How do gain and loss both drain our energy? When you gain, you have to hold on to it. When you lose, you lament what is gone.
How do hope and regret
both steal the present moment?
Hopes for the future can leave us discontented. Regret is a fool’s errand,
as the past can’t be rewritten.
Therefore, the alchemist is content with what he has.
If he thinks of the past,
the focus is on lessons learned.
Rather than regret past mistakes, He can focus on love for others And forgiveness of self
When thoughts of the past arise.
Keep your mind with your body, Allow true virtue to arise.

Can You Yield Until Your Mind is Clear?

Their minds were deep
and they kept their skills hidden.
Because their minds can’t be fathomed and their skills were hidden,
How can we understand them?
They were careful, like one standing on slippery rocks. They were alert, like a sniper
looking through his rifle’s scope.
They were polite, like a visitor in a foreign land.
They flowed like an ancient river.
They were as flexible as the potter’s clay. They bent like the willow in the storm, Their minds were as clear as
A mirror reflecting the summer night.
Can you yield, give, and bend until your mind is clear? Can you exhibit the patience needed,
To allow inner virtue to arise by itself?
One who merges with the Tao
Doesn’t seek to enforce his will.
By letting things take their natural course,

And in the body, this means that the yang qi circulates around the center or core and has the function of protecting the body.

Huang Di continued, “Living in a cold climate, one must take care with one’s activities. Just as people indoors are protected from the weather, the yang qi acts as the walls in a house to protect the body. It is important to be aware, and not allow any openings; pathogenic energy cannot invade if the castle doors are closed.” -The Yellow Emperor’s Classic

“The key to mastering health is to regulate the yin and the yang of the body. If the yin and yang balance is disrupted, it is like going through a year with Spring but no Winter, or Winter but no Summer. When the yang is excessive and cannot contain itself, the yin will become consumed. Only when yin remains calm and harmonious will the yang qi be contained and not be overly expansive. The spirit will be normal and the mind clear. If the yin and yang separate, the jing/essence and the shen/spirit will also leave each other.

“The source and preservation of yin come from the five flavors of food in the diet, but improper use of the five flavors may also injure the five zang organs. Too much sour taste may cause overactivity of the Liver and underactivity of the Spleen. Too much salty taste can weaken the bones and muscles, and stagnate the Heart qi. Too much sweet taste can disturb the Heart qi, causing it to become restless and congested, as well as cause imbalance in the Kidney energy. Too much bitter taste disrupts the Spleen’s ability to transform and transport food, and causes the Stomach to digest poorly, and swell.

“Therefore, one should be mindful of what one consumes to insure proper growth, reproduction, and development of bones, tendons, ligaments, and meridians of acupuncture. This will help generate the smooth flow of qi and blood, enabling one to live to a ripe age.” -The Yellow Emperor’s Classic on Internal Medicine
